findings.message: The project can be taken as one VPC's boundary only if every resource that names a VPC provably names the estate's one, and this estate does not show it: a resource of the estate (a subnet, route table, security group, network ACL, flow log, peering connection, a Cloud Control twin of those, ...) names a VPC by a literal id, a variable, a data source, an attribute of a VPC other than its id (its arn, its owner id, ...) or an expression the scan cannot reduce to one reference to the VPC the estate creates (or the estate creates no VPC of its own). A unit placed in a subnet that the scan cannot show is one of the estate's (a server, load balancer, function or NAT gateway in a subnet given by a variable, a data source or a literal id) is in the same position: it may stand in another VPC. The draft puts every network, security group and routing table in the one var.project_id and cannot say that they all belong to one VPC. Confirm which VPC each of them is in, and whether the networks of another VPC belong in this project or in a project of their own joined through a Network Area. No unit of the VPC topology is automation-eligible until then (gate blocker TOPOLOGY:vpc-unproven).

The scan cannot say which route table is the main route table of this VPC: the VPC has count or for_each (or may be absent), an aws_main_route_table_association may name it through a value the scan cannot resolve (a variable, a literal ID, a conditional, a value from a module call), two resources set it (two main associations, or a main association and an aws_default_route_table on one VPC, which the provider documents as conflicting), or the table is a variable or lies outside the configuration. node.vpc_main_table carries the cause. Which table the VPC's subnets follow without an association of their own, and so what their routing and exposure are, is not decided here; the draft attaches no routing table through the main table.

The adopted default security group states no ingress rule. The AWS provider removes every rule of the default group when it adopts it and creates only the stated ones, so after apply the group allows no inbound traffic at all, not even from the members of the group itself. A new STACKIT security group allows no incoming traffic either, not even between its own members: they reach each other only through a rule whose remote_security_group_id is the group (tested on a STACKIT project on 2026-10-08, IPv4; the concepts page sentence that traffic from the same group is allowed holds for the project's default group, which carries explicit rules for its own members, not for a group you create), so in the ingress direction an empty STACKIT group equals the adopted group. IPv6 between members is not established (no IPv6 network could be created in the probed project). Nothing is drafted for the adopted group: decide which servers relied on the default group and attach them to a STACKIT group that states no ingress rule, not to the project's default group, whose own-member rules would admit its members.

The adopted default security group states no egress rule. The AWS provider removes every rule of the default group when it adopts it and creates only the stated ones, so after apply the group allows no outbound traffic at all (the provider page calls this denying all egress by omitting the rules). A new STACKIT security group allows all outgoing traffic, so a server that moves onto a STACKIT group is wider than the source unless the allow-all egress rules are deleted after apply.

findings.message: Storage is encrypted at rest with an AWS-managed key. STACKIT MariaDB lists "data-at-rest encryption" as a feature, but a sandbox instance (MariaDB 10.11, 2026-09-24) had database-level encryption off (innodb_encrypt_tables, innodb_encrypt_log, encrypt_binlog, aria_encrypt_tables = OFF); whether the volumes beneath are encrypted cannot be observed from a client and is not stated: no STACKIT fact is documented, so it is UNKNOWN and is not relied on.

The source engine is MySQL 8 and its accounts do not move. MySQL 8.0's default authentication plugin is caching_sha2_password (system variable default_authentication_plugin), MariaDB 10.11's default is mysql_native_password or unix_socket; users created with MySQL's SHA256 password algorithm cannot be used in MariaDB 10.11 (MDEV-9804), and a caching_sha2_password plugin exists in MariaDB Community Server only from 11.4.9, 11.8.4 and 12.1 and is not installed by default, while STACKIT offers MariaDB 10.11 (catalogue 2026-10-18). Create the accounts on the target and check that every client library authenticates with a plugin MariaDB 10.11 offers: a client setting that requires caching_sha2_password cannot connect.

MariaDB stores JSON as text, not in a binary format as MySQL: its JSON data type is an alias for LONGTEXT, so the JSON columns of the source become text columns and JSON values are compared as strings, where MySQL compares them as JSON values. MariaDB 10.11 does not support MySQL's JSON operators -> and ->> (MDEV-13594): a query that uses them is rewritten with the JSON functions (JSON_EXTRACT, JSON_UNQUOTE); JSON_SEARCH given invalid data returns NULL and a warning where MySQL raises an error.

The defaults of the character set and the collation differ: MySQL 8.0 uses utf8mb4 and utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, MariaDB 10.11 uses latin1 or utf8 and latin1_swedish_ci or utf8_general_ci, and MariaDB names utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci as the counterpart default only from 11.4. Not all character sets and collations exist in both products, and the pages read do not list utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci as a MariaDB 10.11 collation: check every collation the schema, the dump and the queries name with SHOW COLLATION on the target, and set the character set of every database explicitly.

The default sql_mode differs: MySQL 8.0 sets ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, NO_ZERO_IN_DATE, NO_ZERO_DATE, ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO and NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION; MariaDB 10.11 sets STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO, NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER and NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION. Without ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY the GROUP BY semantics the queries rely on are not enforced the way MySQL enforces them, and zero dates and zero parts in dates are no longer refused by default. A parameter group of the source may set sql_mode itself, and whether the STACKIT instance lets sql_mode be set is not established here: test the queries and the inserts against the target.

Common table expressions (non-recursive and recursive) and window functions are supported by both products (window functions since MariaDB 10.2, per MariaDB's compatibility matrix), so no incompatibility is documented for them; the queries are tested anyway. Documented differences in queries: MariaDB 10.11 does not support lateral derived tables (MDEV-19078) or the MAX_EXECUTION_TIME optimizer hint, and the function VALUES() is called VALUE(); INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS has slightly different fields and the role views differ; the performance schema is off by default in MariaDB 10.11 and on in MySQL. Generated columns are compatible: tables created with MySQL 5.7 or later that hold generated columns import into MariaDB, and STORED is an alias of PERSISTENT.

findings.message: Trust policy: lambda.amazonaws.com or ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com assumes this role, so an application workload (a Lambda function or an ECS task) runs as it. On STACKIT the workload runs as a service account (stackit_service_account) and nothing assumes it: it authenticates with a service account key (stackit_service_account_key, key flow) or, on SKE, by Workload Identity Federation (a federated identity provider on the account). What to decide: key or federation, and the roles of the attached policies (see the permission findings of this unit).

Managed policy of an ECS role (AWS: task execution pulls images from ECR and writes CloudWatch Logs; the container-instance role registers hosts with ECS). STACKIT has no ECS: image pull is a registry credential (Container Registry roles, Guest is read-only) and log shipping a platform or credential setting (stackit_logs_access_token); no STACKIT role replaces these grants. Container Registry: STACKIT offers this service. A public STACKIT API exists for it. The pinned Terraform provider has no resource for it. StackToIT does not draft automation for it yet; extra implementation is needed. (schema checked 2026-10-11: none of the 115 resource types of the pinned STACKIT provider), so the pull credential is not drafted (project roles: docs.stackit.cloud, updated Jul 2, 2026). What to decide: the registry pull credential and the log destination of the replacing workload.

A policy of this role grants KMS actions. STACKIT KMS access comes from role assignments on an organisation, folder, project or service account, not on a key ring or key (stackit_kms_key has no policy or grant attribute in the pinned STACKIT provider), so a per-key permission widens to every key of the project. What to decide: which identities may use and which may administer keys, and whether keys that need different access move to their own project.

A policy of this role reads or writes secrets or parameters. STACKIT Secrets Manager grants access with role bindings on the instance and on secret groups (stackit_secretsmanager_instance_role_binding_v1, stackit_secretsmanager_secret_group_role_binding_v1; documented roles Secrets Manager Reader and Admin) and with users that carry credentials. What to decide: per secret group, which identity reads and which writes. One more limit exists per instance: a source-address list (stackit_secretsmanager_instance acls, IP addresses or CIDR ranges that may reach the instance), the nearest thing to an aws:SourceIp condition; there is no per-identity or per-secret condition.

findings.message: The value of this record changes with the migration, and its three effects are kept apart: the address change, the reachability and the effect on what depends on the address. Address change: the record points at an address or a name that belongs to an AWS resource the migration replaces (an instance or Elastic IP address, a load balancer, a CloudFront distribution, an S3 website, or a value built from one of them); on STACKIT it has to point at the generated STACKIT resource (a public IP address, a load balancer address), which exists only after apply: the draft writes that reference where the source proves which resource it is and otherwise asks for the value in a variable. Reachability: the new address answers only once the STACKIT resource is up and the record is switched to it, and an AAAA value is reachable only through the IPv6 arrangement of the finding for AAAA records. Effect on what depends on the address: firewalls and allow-lists of partners, certificates validated against the old name or address, health checks and clients that hold the old address are not visible in the source and follow the record by hand. The record is therefore never carried as a like-for-like move, whatever the other records of its zone do.

target.service: none - no packet-flow log: a capture on the servers whose records a log shipper sends to a STACKIT Logs instance is a design of its own

result.reason: A flow log records the IP traffic of a VPC, subnet or network interface (accepted, rejected or both) and delivers it to a log group, a bucket or a stream through a delivery role. STACKIT has no counterpart: the provider has no flow-log resource (the pinned provider schema) and the documentation read describes no record of network traffic; the STACKIT Audit Log covers API and control-plane events, not packet flows. What replaces it is a design of its own that StackToIT does not draft: a capture on the servers themselves (the firewall or connection-tracking log of each server, or a flow exporter) whose records a log shipper sends to a STACKIT Logs instance (written over OTLP; a Logs access token with the write permission lets the shipper authenticate). A capture on the servers sees what reaches a server; the documentation read states no log of the traffic the security groups drop, so a capture of rejected traffic has no documented counterpart. The log group the flow log wrote to is a unit of its own that maps to a Logs instance, which can receive the records of the replacement; a bucket or a stream as destination is a decision of its own. result.reason: STACKIT has no stateless subnet ACLs: there is no network ACL resource, and in a Network Area access control at network level is carried out exclusively by security groups. Security groups work on an allow-list basis with default deny; a rule has a direction, protocol, port range and address range and no action and no rule number, so a deny entry of the ACL and the rule-number order that makes it win cannot be expressed. The rules of all groups are evaluated simultaneously, in no order, and the groups attached to one network interface are aggregated permissively (if one group allows traffic and another does not mention it, the traffic is allowed), so a group can add access and never take it away. A stateless security group exists in the API and the provider but is still allow-only, so it is no deny-capable ACL either. The Unified Firewall (generally available since 2026-07-07) aggregates the settings of security groups, database ACLs and public IP configurations and does not replace them; the pinned provider has no resource for it. A next-generation firewall is announced for 2026 only. Deny rules and subnet-level filtering therefore have to be re-expressed as security-group allow rules or a firewall appliance the customer runs. A network ACL is a ceiling on top of the security groups, not a grant, and the security groups attached to one STACKIT network interface are aggregated (the more permissive rule wins): a group written from the ACL's allow rules and attached to the servers would open every port the ACL allows, also where the servers' own groups do not, so the ceiling is carried only by narrowing the rules of those groups (or a firewall appliance), never by adding a group.

result.reason: A route of the table sends traffic to a NAT gateway (the others, if any, to an internet gateway), and the draft's project is outside a Network Area. Observed on the target (tested on a STACKIT project in eu01 on 2026-10-10, a project outside a Network Area): a routed STACKIT network gives servers with and without a public IP the same outbound reachability with no route and no routing table, nothing initiated from the internet reaches a server behind the network address, and egress is restricted by the egress rules of security groups. The table is therefore not drafted: STACKIT's default routing replaces it. What a NAT gateway has beyond an internet route is NOT CARRIED and stays an open review: the gateway's fixed egress address is LOST (observed: the address a routed network leaves by is its project's publicIp, one address for every routed network of the project, not fixed - it changed after every network of the project was deleted, twice - and not settable, a PATCH answers 202 and is ignored), so a third party's allow-list on the NAT gateway's address does not survive and needs a STACKIT public IP per server (the only address the probe saw stay fixed); the restriction of egress to the gateway is carried only by security-group egress rules, which the draft does not tie to this table; the absence of an inbound path is observed. LOW: the loss is for a person to decide, as the plan decision NAT_FIXED_EGRESS_ADDRESS_LOST. The egress itself is not widened where the gateway is a public one: the subnets of this table reached the internet through it in the source, so the plan decision EXPOSURE_WIDENED_EGRESS (a subnet whose source had no route to the internet; a subnet behind a private NAT gateway is one, a private gateway gives no internet access) is not what this table raises; what changes is the address. STACKIT documents the way out as source NAT of the network (Virtual Network concepts, last updated Mar 11, 2026). Which NAT gateway the route names does not change this: a table that picks its NAT gateway by an index (one gateway per availability zone) or by a conditional between NAT gateways is decided as a table with one plain reference, because every gateway it can name is lost the same way and STACKIT has no NAT gateway to pick. A Gateway endpoint of S3 or DynamoDB that names the table adds a route that is NOT CARRIED (Object Storage is reached over the network's default path); it does not change the case, a check on the gateway endpoint names it. The destinations are read by the check of the route destinations. (Whether deps[3] (module.vpc.module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.private's count/for_each is not known statically (it may not exist)) exist was evaluated for each possibility; the mapping decides the same either way.)

result.reason: Every route of the table sends traffic to an internet gateway (a reference to an aws_internet_gateway, or an ID that is not a virtual private gateway's) and the draft's project is outside a Network Area. Observed on the target (tested on a STACKIT project in eu01 on 2026-10-10, a project outside a Network Area): a routed STACKIT network gives servers with and without a public IP the same outbound reachability with no route and no routing table configured (HTTPS, ICMP, DNS and TCP 443 in 62 of 62 rounds over 30 minutes per server; a non-routed network reaches nothing), nothing initiated from the internet reaches a server behind the network address (tcp 22, 80, 8080 timed out in 137 of 137 samples with an admitting security group), egress is restricted by the egress rules of security groups, and routed networks reach each other with no table. The table is therefore not drafted: STACKIT's default routing replaces it. Equivalent for a server that has a public IP. NOT equivalent for a server WITHOUT one: in the source an internet gateway serves only an instance with a public IPv4 or Elastic IP address ("the instances in the public subnet must have public IP addresses or Elastic IP addresses to enable communication with the internet over the internet gateway", AWS internet gateway documentation), so such an instance has no internet path; on STACKIT the same server leaves through the SNAT address of its network (observed in the STACKIT sandbox on two rounds; "VM without one: the SNAT address of its network, shared by every VM in that network without its own public IP", stackitcloud/professional-service examples/vpn-full-tunnel-central-egress README). The draft therefore GIVES egress to servers the source did not give it; the table does not carry that, and it is decided on the subnet (the finding that the egress of the subnet is not proven, and the plan decision EXPOSURE_WIDENED_EGRESS of the subnet, private egress ipv4), not here. What the STACKIT documentation says of the same behaviour (Virtual Network concepts, last updated Mar 11, 2026, read 2026-10-27): "Every subnet is routed to the public internet. Technically this is done by source NAT (SNAT) in combination with masquerading", it "supports outbound internet access but does not allow traffic initiated from the public internet to reach your resources", and the routing "can be controlled using Routing tables" only for projects that are part of a Network Area. So outside an area the equivalence rests on the documentation and on the test of 2026-10-10, which agree. Not HIGH: the test was one project, one region, one day, no probe in a Network Area (a draft that writes a Network Area is the case of a table in a Network Area), and the servers without a public IP are not equivalent (above). The destinations are read by the check of the route destinations: only 0.0.0.0/0 is default routing, any other destination (IPv6 included) is REVIEW. A Gateway endpoint of S3 or DynamoDB that names the table adds a route that is NOT CARRIED and does not change the case. target.service: none - no account guardrail; exposure is set by security groups and by who may attach public IPs

result.reason: The setting blocks internet gateway traffic for every VPC of the account in the Region: block-bidirectional (no traffic in or out through internet gateways), block-ingress (outbound allowed) or off. STACKIT has no such guardrail. Inbound access is denied by default by security groups (docs: 'all incoming traffic is denied by default') and a server is reachable from the internet only through a public IP, which is created and attached through the IAM-authorised actions iaas.public-ip.create and iaas.server.public-ip.add; the replacement is a role set that withholds those actions plus security groups without internet-wide ingress rules. Outbound traffic of a routed network leaves through the router's source NAT (docs.stackit.cloud architecture page; observed in the test of 2026-10-10 of this knowledge base) and no schema attribute blocks it, so block-bidirectional cannot be expressed as a setting.
review: Decide who may create and attach public IPs in the STACKIT project and keep security groups free of internet-wide ingress rules; outbound blocking has no setting.
